review_first.title: The close seam (card 1)
review_first.text: Every approval goes through it. It is where the one open correctness risk sits (a concurrent double create), and the next ticket category will plug in there too.

architecture.title: Closing a ticket gets a seam with two adapters

before.text: The close endpoint holds the change-request rules itself: a ChangeRequest is validated, applied and JSON-sniffed for new users in its own transaction; everything else is just Close + Save. A new ticket category meant another branch in the endpoint.

after.mermaid:
flowchart TB E[Close endpoint] --> V[ticket.ValidateClose] V --> S{{IRegisterTicketApplier
Handles · ValidateCloseAsync ·
RequiresTransaction · ApplyAsync}} S --> A1[RegisterChange-
RequestApplier] S --> A2[NewEntity-
RequestApplier] E --> P[after commit: provisioning mail,
Geposit, events]

architecture.problem: On main the close endpoint holds the change-request rules itself, so every category is a new branch there.
architecture.solution: The endpoint validates, opens the transaction only when RequiresTransaction says so, and dispatches on Handles(category).
wins: Two adapters make it a real seam
Locality: each category's close rules sit in one module
architecture.risk: Review finding 2 (Should fix, plausible): two concurrent closes as Godkänd can each pass validation and create the operation and control ticket twice (CloseRegisterTicketEndpoint.cs:51).

architecture.title: Creating suppliers and operations moves into Library

before.text: POST /operations and POST /suppliers each create the entity and provision its users inline. Six places choose internal vs external accounts themselves: both create endpoints, UpdateSupplierEndpoint:61, OperationContactPersonsEndpointBase:57, OperationFieldApplier:200 and SupplierFieldApplier:51 (on main).

after.mermaid:
flowchart LR O[POST /operations] --> OC S[POST /suppliers] --> SC AP[NewEntityRequestApplier] --> OC & SC OC[OperationCreator] --> U SC[SupplierCreator] --> U CP[contact-person endpoints,
SupplierFieldApplier] --> U U[PriisUserManager
.CreateSupplierUsersAsync]

architecture.problem: Approving a request has to create exactly what the create endpoints create, but on main that logic lives inside API endpoints.
architecture.solution: One creator per entity in Library, called by the endpoint and by the applier; the account-type rule lives in one method.
wins: Leverage: one interface, three call sites
Approval and create can't drift apart
Provisioning rule in one place (5 callers)
architecture.risk: SupplierCreator is a stopgap: #31429 moves it to BaseSupplier.AsyncMutations.CreateAsync (SupplierCreator.cs:28). POST /operations and POST /suppliers stay off ExtendedCreateEndpoint because provisioning needs a transaction scope (fastendpoints skill §7).

architecture.title: RegisterTicketNewEntityRequest: a 1:1 detail on the ticket

after.text: Lifecycle of the detail row. Submitted: ProposalJson plus typed columns (parent supplier or proposed org number, proposed category, IVO answer). Decided: DecisionJson, DecisionSavedOn, decided category and org number, DecidedPermitFileId. Converted (Godkänd): RecordConversion stores the created supplier, operation and control ticket ids and clears the permit file id, because the operation owns it now. Closed otherwise: ReleaseDecidedPermitFile deletes the file in the close's save.

architecture.problem: The request has to be searched, filtered for protected data and checked for duplicates, but most of its fields are only read back.
architecture.solution: Columns for what is queried, JSON for the rest (D6). CanBeApprovedExpression (:100) is shared by the profile and the list.
wins: One owner for the permit file
Temporal table, like the other register tables
architecture.risk: Review findings 3 and 5: Deserialize swallows a JsonException (NewEntityDecision.cs:41), and IsProtectedHousing claims to be the only definition while the filter SQL and ProtectedSubject restate it (RegisterTicketNewEntityRequest.cs:89).

architecture.title: The API: four new endpoints, three new SystemActions

sequenceDiagram
  actor F as Faisal (OperationManager)
  actor A as Amalia (RegisterAdministrator)
  participant API
  F->>API: POST /register-tickets/new-operation-requests (11021)
  F->>API: POST /register-tickets/new-supplier-with-operation-requests (11022)
  API-->>F: register ticket created
  A->>API: PUT /register-tickets/{id}/new-entity-request/decision (11051, multipart)
  A->>API: GET …/new-entity-request/permit-file (11051)

architecture.problem: Only operation managers may send a request (D4, D18), and only the register administrator may see the decision and its permit file.
architecture.solution: Separate actions for request and decision. The permit-file endpoint reuses 11051 as its policy, and GET /files/{id} refuses decided permit files.
wins: Contract traced across the halves: consistent
architecture.risk: Review finding 1 (Should fix, Security): the created supplier and operation show as links that the requester may not be allowed to open (NewEntityRequestDto.cs:61 ↔ new-entity-request-section.tsx:495). Finding 8: the PR description says the requester doesn't see the decision, but since 239b8e401 they do.

architecture.title: After the commit: accounts, mail and control-ticket events

after.mermaid:
flowchart TB C[Commit: supplier, operation,
control ticket and accounts saved] --> M[Provisioning mail to every
account created during the apply] C --> N[RegisterTicketClosedEvent to Faisal;
control-ticket number only when shared] C --> L[ControlTicketLifecycle.PublishCreatedAsync]

architecture.problem: A mail or event sent before the commit would announce entities that a rollback could remove.
architecture.solution: The applier returns an outcome, and the endpoint acts on it only after Complete(). ControlTicketLifecycle is also used by POST /control-tickets.
wins: Nothing is announced before the commit

architecture.title: Frontend: two wizards built from existing steps

before.text: Three wizards ask for nearly the same operation fields, each with its own rules for what is required.

after.text: One set of operation steps in three modes (CreateOperationContext.mode): create (POST /operations), request (Faisal; IVO question only) and decide (Amalia; permit and file). The decision wizard reuses SupplierFormFields and ControlStartAndShareFields; supplier and operation default to Paused (schema.ts:126, :133).

architecture.problem: Three wizards ask for nearly the same operation fields with different rules for what is required.
architecture.solution: One set of steps with request* / decide* variants. The mode decides what is asked and what is required. The close dialog offers Godkänd only when canBeApproved is true.
wins: Approval gate mirrors the API rule
architecture.risk: Review findings 10–12: the "no permit download" e2e assertion can't fail (new-entity-request.spec.ts:223), several UI paths have no spec, and the decision transform uses `as` casts (schema.ts:235).

rows.text: Two variants for a logged-in operation manager
Decision creates nothing; Godkänd creates everything in one transaction
Fields starred in the form are required, the rest optional
Only the operation manager role may submit
Target: A = the supplier; B = none, named after the proposed supplier
Typed columns for what is searched or linked, JSON for the rest
An existing org number blocks Godkänd; other open requests shown as info only
Supplier and operation Pausad by default
rows.evidence: FE/…/decide-new-entity-request/schema.ts:126, :133 (the API requires an explicit status; the default is only in the UI)

rows.text: Godkänd only with a saved decision; a past start date becomes today
Provisioning mail; a variant of "Kontroll påbörjad"
rows.evidence: CloseRegisterTicketEndpoint.cs:90–91, :102–103 (no test for the mail, review finding 9)
No such field in the request or decision files

rows.text: IVO answer: Ja / Nej / Ej tillståndspliktig
Shared control ticket is linked in the closed notification
Unshared control ticket: its number never reaches the requester
Close dialog hides Godkänd when the org number exists
"Ditt konto har skapats" also when the ticket is not shared

Links to entities the requester can't open
